components.css: .ds-tray { background: var(--color-tray-bg, #141820); border: 1px solid var(--color-border, #29303e); border-radius: 14px; padding: 8px; box-shadow: var(--shadow-tray, inset 0 2px 10px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.42)); font-family: var(--font-sans, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'SF Pro Text', Roboto, sans-serif); } .ds-grid { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(6, minmax(0, 1fr)); border: 2px solid var(--color-grid-box, #8a95a8); border-radius: 7px; overflow: hidden; background: var(--color-surface, #181c24); font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; } .ds-cell { height: 34px; display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; font-size: 0.9375rem; font-weight: 700; color: var(--color-given, #f7f5f0); border-right: 1px solid var(--color-grid-cell, #262d3a); border-bottom: 1px solid var(--color-grid-cell, #262d3a); } .ds-cell:nth-child(6n) { border-right: none; } .ds-cell:nth-child(n + 7) { border-bottom: none; } .ds-br { border-right: 2px solid var(--color-grid-box, #8a95a8); } .ds-bb { border-bottom: 2px solid var(--color-grid-box, #8a95a8); } .ds-peer { background: var(--color-peer, #1d2534); } .ds-sel { background: var(--color-selected-cell, #1e365c); color: var(--color-primary-text, #60a5fa); outline: 2px solid var(--color-focus, #60a5fa); outline-offset: -2px; } .ds-user { color: var(--color-user, #60a5fa); font-weight: 600; } .ds-partner { color: var(--color-partner, #c084fc); background: var(--color-partner-bg, rgba(192, 132, 252, 0.14)); font-weight: 600; } .ds-hint { color: var(--color-hint, #fbbf24); background: var(--color-hint-bg, rgba(251, 191, 36, 0.15)); }

components.css: .ds-numpad { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(3, 56px); gap: 6px; font-family: var(--font-sans, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'SF Pro Text', Roboto, sans-serif); } .ds-key { min-height: 50px; padding: 4px 0; display: flex; flex-direction: column; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 2px; background: var(--color-surface, #181c24); border: 1px solid var(--color-border, #29303e); border-radius: 10px; color: var(--color-primary-text, #60a5fa); font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; cursor: pointer; transition: background-color 120ms ease, transform 100ms ease, border-color 120ms ease; } .ds-key:hover:not(:disabled) { background: var(--color-surface-hover, #2a3140); border-color: var(--color-primary, #2563eb); } .ds-key:active:not(:disabled) { transform: scale(0.96); } .ds-key:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid var(--color-focus, #60a5fa); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-key--active { background: var(--color-active-tool-bg, rgba(96, 165, 250, 0.18)); border-color: var(--color-primary, #2563eb); } .ds-key--done { opacity: 0.4; cursor: not-allowed; } .ds-key-digit { font-size: 1.125rem; font-weight: 700; line-height: 1; } .ds-key-count { font-size: 0.65rem; font-weight: 600; color: var(--color-text-muted, #a6b0bf); min-height: 12px; display: inline-flex; align-items: center; }

narrative.overview:
Sudoku Shift is an Operate-mode puzzle environment that pairs a genuine native Framework7 (`theme="auto"`) application shell—adapting automatically to Cupertino on iOS/macOS and Material Design on Android and Desktop—with the tactile precision of a recessed enamel board tray and tournament chess clock. Navigation, inset grouped lists, segmented controls, and dialogs behave with immediate platform predictability, while the active Sudoku board sits inside an inset tray where row/column/box crosshairs, matching-digit echoes, and live co-op partner cursors read in a single glance.

The visual system runs across two first-class palettes that sync with OS appearance (`system`, `dark`, `light`) via `data-theme` and a `.dark` bridge on `documentElement`: Night Enamel (deep obsidian enamel with bone-ivory ink for evening focus) and Bone Ivory (warm paper canvas with crisp white inset cards for daylight reading). An opt-in 1981 C64 Retro Mode (`[data-retro="true"]`, unlocked via Konami code) intentionally breaks from the studio shell into a zero-radius, scanlined 8-bit pixel world. Generic flat-grey puzzle clones, decorative gradient title fills, and web-div imitations of native chrome are explicitly rejected in favor of high-contrast functional clarity and WCAG 2.2 AA rigor.
keyCharacteristics: Native Framework7 `theme="auto"` chrome bridged directly to Enamel semantic tokens (`--f7-theme-color`, `--f7-page-bg-color`, `--f7-bars-bg-color`, `--f7-list-bg-color`, `--f7-card-bg-color`).
Recessed enamel board tray with inset depth, 2px box boundaries, 1px internal hairlines, and tabular-aligned coordinate axes.

Role-coded gameplay signals separating givens (neutral ink), player moves (cobalt), co-op partner moves and cursors (royal iris), logical/spectator hints (brass amber), solved units (emerald), and conflicts (coral/crimson).
Equal-pane responsive geometry engineered for phones, tablets, desktops, itch.io embeds, and dual-screen foldables with hinge avoidance.
Strict accessibility and motion discipline with a 44px minimum touch floor, compositor-only animations, intentional `prefers-reduced-motion` replacements, and `forced-colors` support.

rules.name: The Split-Accent Contrast Rule
rules.body: Filled buttons use saturated Tournament Cobalt (#2563eb dark / #1d4ed8 light) with white ink, whereas text, icons, focus rings, and user digits on dark surfaces always switch to Cobalt Luminous (#60a5fa) so every interactive label clears WCAG AA without glowing.

rules.name: The Ownership Separation Rule
rules.body: Given digits remain neutral ink, self moves own Cobalt, co-op partner moves and cursors own Royal Iris, and hints own Brass Amber. Never cross-assign these hues across roles.

rules.name: The Artwork Scrim Rule
rules.body: Progressive board artwork sits behind cells at 0.12 opacity until solved and only illuminates cell-by-cell through calibrated reveal scrims (--color-reveal-scrim / --color-reveal-unit-scrim), guaranteeing digits never lose contrast against photographic color.

rules.name: The Tabular Digits Rule
rules.body: Every numeric readout—board cells, coordinate axes, numpad remaining counters, live room progress (filled/total), timers, volume percentages, and solve contribution tables—must declare font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums so numbers never jitter as counts change.

rules.name: The Single H1 Landmark Rule
rules.body: Every route renders one <main> landmark and one <h1> (visually prominent on Setup, Watch, Settings, and Legal; .sr-only on Gameplay so the board owns the entire viewport).

rules.name: The Recessed Board Rule
rules.body: The Sudoku grid sits inside a sunken tray (--color-tray-bg + --shadow-tray) while cards and dialogs sit above the canvas; never place the active grid flat on bare canvas without its recessed tray.

rules.name: The Compositor-Only Motion Rule
rules.body: Transitions and keyframes animate transform, opacity, and subtle color/border shifts only (100ms–250ms ease for controls; cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1) for unit celebrations, hints, and solve reveals). Under @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce), all vestibular transforms, floats, rotations, and Framework7 ripples disable while preserving static high-contrast hint, selection, and solved states (never a blunt global 0.01ms kill-switch).

dos: Do route all native shell controls through Framework7 theme="auto" classes and bridge them to the Enamel CSS custom properties (--f7-theme-color, --f7-page-bg-color, --f7-bars-bg-color, --f7-list-bg-color) rather than hardcoding platform colors.

Do keep dark-mode text, icons, focus outlines, and user digits on Cobalt Luminous (#60a5fa via --color-primary-text / --color-focus) while reserving saturated Tournament Cobalt (#2563eb) for filled button surfaces with white ink.
Do apply font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums to every numeric cell, counter, axis, timer, and results table.
Do enclose Sudoku grids and setup previews inside a recessed tray (--color-tray-bg + --shadow-tray) with 2px box boundaries and 1px cell hairlines.
Do maintain the 44px (--touch-min) minimum touch floor across every button, tab, segmented radio option, input, select, and slider.
Do use drawn inline SVG icons (1.9px–2px round-cap stroke) for navigation, arrows, search, checkmarks, and settings controls.
Do pair every new animation with a purposeful non-vestibular fallback inside @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) and preserve semantic outlines inside @media (forced-colors: active).
donts: Don't apply gradient text fills, glowing shadows, or decorative chrome to headings, buttons, or the Sudoku board.
Don't reuse Royal Iris (#c084fc / #7c3aed) or Brass Amber (#fbbf24 / #9a4406) for general primary navigation or self actions; keep them strictly scoped to co-op partner presence and hint signals.
Don't substitute raw Unicode glyphs (←, →, ✓, ↑, ↓) for UI chrome icons; emoji belong only to domain-level spectator reactions and the Co-op Fist Bump Easter egg.
Don't break the .split-panes equal-track grid or omit env(safe-area-inset-*) and viewport-segment-* hinge variables when adding new views or overlays.
Don't leak 1981 C64 Retro Mode styling (0px radii, 4px 4px 0 offset shadows, scanlines, Courier monospace) outside [data-retro="true"].
Don't add a global * { animation-duration: 0.01ms !important } override; keep reduced-motion fallbacks explicit and legible.
